UnitStatement: The `four-documents` brief schema defines the INIT-TASK dispatch contract for `TASK + four-documents`.
Use `four-documents` when ORCHESTRATOR needs the standard four-document kit drafted or enriched for one PROJECT or SOFTWARE deliverable.
For `four-documents`, `ScopePath` should be the target deliverable folder.
`AllowedWriteTargets` for `four-documents` should be limited to the four kit documents plus `_STATUS.md` when a safe state transition is expected.
The `PURPOSE` brief field is a required string explaining why a `four-documents` run exists.
The `ScopePath` brief field is a required path to the deliverable-local folder.
The `TaskSkill` brief field must equal `four-documents` for this skill.
The `AllowedWriteTargets` brief field lists the kit-document outputs and optional `_STATUS.md`.
`RuntimeOverrides.DELIVERABLE_PATH` is a required path to the deliverable folder.
`RuntimeOverrides.DECOMPOSITION_REF` is a required path to the decomposition reference.
`RuntimeOverrides.RUN_PASSES` is a required enum selecting which passes to run.
`ExpectedOutputs` is a required list of required outputs for the run.
`RuntimeOverrides.ALLOW_OVERWRITE_STATES` is an optional safe-write state gate.
`RuntimeOverrides.OBJECTIVE_ASSOCIATION_MODE` is an optional objective-association mode.
`RuntimeOverrides.DECOMP_VARIANT` is an optional enum for the originating decomposition variant.
`CustomInstructions` should contain only run-specific emphasis.
`DECOMP_VARIANT=DOMAIN` is invalid for `four-documents`.
`RUN_PASSES=P3_ONLY` requires the four existing documents plus `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` to already exist.
`AllowedWriteTargets` should not widen beyond the deliverable folder.
After a successful Pass 1 `four-documents` run, the four document files must exist.
`DECOMP_VARIANT=DOMAIN` must be rejected with `UNSUPPORTED_VARIANT`.
`P3_ONLY` must not proceed unless the four existing documents and `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` are already present.
A `four-documents` run must not modify metadata files other than the safe `_STATUS.md` update.
Source-grounding gaps must appear as `TBD`, assumptions, or conflict-table entries rather than invented content.
A `four-documents` run must stay within the target deliverable folder.
Every warranted item ID in `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` must have a Pass 3 disposition, with no stale or nonexistent item IDs referenced.
`python3 tools/validation/validate_p3_disposition.py {DELIVERABLE_PATH}` must pass before Pass 3 output is accepted.
`FAILED_INPUTS` is used when authoritative source materials are unavailable.
`FAILED_INPUTS` is used when required existing files for `P3_ONLY` are missing.
`FAILED_INPUTS` is used when overwrite protection blocks the run.
`UNSUPPORTED_VARIANT` is used when `DECOMP_VARIANT=DOMAIN`.
The run record must identify inaccessible source materials as missing.
The run record must identify source rereads for substantive Pass 3 changes.
The run record must identify conflict-table additions when source materials and decomposition context disagree.
The run record must provide item-by-item Pass 3 disposition evidence for all warranted `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` rows.
The skill name is `four-documents`.
`four-documents` drafts and iteratively enriches Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, and Procedure documents for a PROJECT or SOFTWARE deliverable.
`four-documents` is compatible with Chirality TASK and is dispatched by the ORCHESTRATOR setup pipeline in Phases 2.2 and 2.5.
The `four-documents` skill metadata declares `chirality-skill-version` as `1`.
The `four-documents` skill metadata declares `chirality-task-profile` as `NONE`.
`four-documents` drafts and enriches four deliverable-local documents for one `PROJECT_DECOMP` or `SOFTWARE_DECOMP` production unit.
`Datasheet.md` is the descriptive document in the four-document kit.
`Specification.md` is the normative document in the four-document kit.
`Guidance.md` is the directional document in the four-document kit.
`Procedure.md` is the operational document in the four-document kit.
`four-documents` can run up to three passes within a single invocation, selected by `RUN_PASSES`.
Pass 1 establishes DOMAIN and TASK, then generates the four documents grounded in accessible sources.
Pass 2 performs a cross-reference consistency check and uses a Conflict Table when needed.
Pass 3 performs semantic lensing enrichment using `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` as a candidate worklist.
The ORCHESTRATOR setup pipeline dispatches `four-documents` twice via TASK.
Phase 2.2 dispatches `four-documents` with `RUN_PASSES: P1_P2` before `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` exists.
Phase 2.5 dispatches `four-documents` with `RUN_PASSES: P3_ONLY` after `lens-register` produces `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md`.
A single `FULL` run is supported for ad-hoc reruns when the lensing register already exists.
`four-documents` does not modify metadata files other than safe `_STATUS.md` updates and does not produce `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md`.
`four-documents` runs in the `TASK` generic shell mode with no profile.
`DELIVERABLE_PATH` is required and must be the absolute path to one production unit folder.
`DECOMPOSITION_REF` is required and must point to decomposition documents or a decomposition folder.
`RUN_PASSES` accepts `FULL`, `P1_P2`, or `P3_ONLY`, with `FULL` as the default.
`ALLOW_OVERWRITE_STATES` defaults to `OPEN, INITIALIZED, SEMANTIC_READY`.
`OBJECTIVE_ASSOCIATION_MODE` defaults to `PACKAGE_HEURISTIC`.
`DECOMP_VARIANT` defaults to `PROJECT`, permits `SOFTWARE`, and rejects `DOMAIN` with `UNSUPPORTED_VARIANT`.
`RUN_PASSES` controls which enrichment passes are run.
`four-documents` is a reasoning-only skill with no required or allowed deterministic tools.
`tools/scaffolding/write_status.sh` may be invoked only for the Step 7 safe `_STATUS.md` update.
`four-documents` forbids writes outside `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}`, except for the status helper writing to the same folder.
`four-documents` forbids modifications to `_CONTEXT.md`, `_DEPENDENCIES.md`, `_REFERENCES.md`, `_MEMORY.md`, `_SEMANTIC.md`, and `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md`.
`four-documents` forbids cross-deliverable scanning or editing.
Authoritative source materials explicitly referenced in `_REFERENCES.md` are the highest-authority sources for drafting or revision.
Deliverable-local reference pointers in `_REFERENCES.md` and `_CONTEXT.md` are the second authority tier for drafting or revision.
The deliverable entry in the decomposition narrative is the third authority tier for drafting or revision.
Existing drafted files are context only and are not authority for drafting or revision.
`_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` is a candidate worklist only and is never authority.
When source material and decomposition narrative disagree, source material is authoritative and the discrepancy is recorded in the Conflict Table.
Do not treat decomposition summaries, prior draft wording, or generic convention as source material when actual source text is locally available.
Step 0 reads `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}/_STATUS.md` when present to determine the current state.
If the current state is outside `ALLOW_OVERWRITE_STATES`, `four-documents` must not overwrite the four documents.
When overwrite protection blocks document writes, `four-documents` returns `RUN_STATUS=SKIPPED_PROTECT_HUMAN_WORK` with the observed state.
`RUN_PASSES=FULL` runs Steps 1 through 7 as written.
`RUN_PASSES=P1_P2` runs Steps 1 through 5 and Step 7, skipping Step 6.
`RUN_PASSES=P3_ONLY` runs minimal context read, Step 6, and a final mini consistency sweep without Pass 1 generation.
`DECOMP_VARIANT=DOMAIN` causes `four-documents` to return `RUN_STATUS=UNSUPPORTED_VARIANT`.
For `P3_ONLY`, the four documents must already exist in the deliverable folder.
For `P3_ONLY`, `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}/_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` must exist.
If a `P3_ONLY` precondition is missing, `four-documents` returns `RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS` and does not modify files.
Step 1 reads `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}/_CONTEXT.md`.
Step 1 extracts deliverable identity, package, discipline, type, responsible party, description, and anticipated artifacts from `_CONTEXT.md`.
Step 1 extracts any pointer to the decomposition entry from `_CONTEXT.md`.
Step 1 reads the deliverable entry in `DECOMPOSITION_REF`, using the pointer when available or locating by deliverable ID.
Step 1 extracts deliverable narrative context, downstream-use hints, explicit requirements, and constraints from the decomposition entry.
Explicit objective-to-deliverable mappings may be recorded as context only when they list the deliverable ID.
`OBJECTIVE_ASSOCIATION_MODE=PACKAGE_HEURISTIC` applies the package-grouping heuristic.
Under the package-grouping heuristic, objective rows mentioning the deliverable package ID are treated as directionally relevant context.
Package-grouping objective associations must be recorded as assumptions and not treated as hard requirements unless confirmed by a human.
Step 1 reads `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}/_REFERENCES.md` to identify reference materials.
Step 1 reads locally accessible reference materials listed in `_REFERENCES.md` as the authoritative source set.
If `_REFERENCES.md` is absent or lists no sources, `four-documents` returns `RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS`.
If no listed reference materials are locally accessible, `four-documents` returns `RUN_STATUS=FAILED_INPUTS`.
If some references are accessible and others are not, `four-documents` proceeds with accessible sources and records inaccessible sources as missing.
Content depending solely on inaccessible source materials becomes `TBD`.
For each accessible source, Step 1 reads source slices relevant to the deliverable scope.
Step 1 reads `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}/_DEPENDENCIES.md` on a best-effort basis.
Only human-declared upstream and downstream dependency lists are used as constraints.
Extracted dependency summaries, run notes, and consumer notes are context only unless explicitly stated as requirements in evidence sources.
Step 2 infers the discipline or domain primarily from `_CONTEXT.md`.
Step 2 identifies candidate standards or codes only from accessible sources.
If a standard is mentioned but unavailable, record it as an assumption and do not derive clause-level requirements.
`Datasheet.md` keeps default schema sections: Identification, Attributes, Conditions, Construction, and References.
`Specification.md` keeps default schema sections: Scope, Requirements, Standards, Verification, and Documentation.
`Guidance.md` keeps default schema sections: Purpose, Principles, Considerations, Trade-offs, and Examples.
`Procedure.md` keeps default schema sections: Purpose, Prerequisites, Steps, Verification, and Records.
Additional sections may be added when required by deliverable type, but default schema sections must not be removed.
Step 3 extracts subject and constraints from `_CONTEXT.md` and the decomposition entry.
Step 3 extracts explicit constraints from accessible references, including design limits, code requirements, and interface boundaries.
Step 3 extracts anticipated artifacts from `_CONTEXT.md`.
All Step 3 inferences must be labeled as assumptions.
Step 4 generates the four documents in `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}` using DOMAIN and TASK.
When authoritative source material is locally accessible, drafted content must be grounded in relevant source slices rather than only decomposition summaries, `_CONTEXT.md`, or generic convention.
`Datasheet.md` Identification is populated from `_CONTEXT.md`.
`Datasheet.md` Attributes, Conditions, and Construction are populated with values explicitly found in sources.
`Datasheet.md` References lists the sources used.
`Datasheet.md` uses `TBD` when information is missing and must not invent values.
`Specification.md` Scope states what the deliverable covers and excludes from `_CONTEXT.md` and decomposition.
`Specification.md` Requirements are derived only from accessible sources; inferred requirements are labeled as assumptions.
`Specification.md` Standards lists governing standards and marks inaccessible locations as `location TBD`.
`Specification.md` Verification maps requirements to verification approaches.
`Specification.md` Documentation lists required artifacts from anticipated artifacts.
`Guidance.md` Purpose states why the deliverable exists from decomposition.
`Guidance.md` Principles, Considerations, and Trade-offs draw rationale from sources or use `TBD`.
`Guidance.md` Examples are only from sources and otherwise omitted or marked `TBD`.
`Guidance.md` creates or updates the Conflict Table when contradictions appear.
`Procedure.md` may describe steps to produce the deliverable artifact, use or operate it, or both, depending on deliverable type and source availability.
`Procedure.md` Prerequisites include declared upstream dependencies and required references.
`Procedure.md` Steps are derived from specification requirements plus deliverable-type conventions, using `TBD` where judgment is needed.
`Procedure.md` Verification checks confirm that steps succeeded.
`Procedure.md` Records state what evidence or documents should result.
Step 5 checks cross-document consistency.
Step 5 verifies that Datasheet entities and attributes are reflected in Specification requirements where appropriate.
Step 5 verifies that Specification requirements have rationale or considerations in Guidance where appropriate.
Step 5 verifies that Specification requirements have verification hooks in Procedure.
Step 5 verifies terminology consistency across all four documents.
Step 5 verifies numeric values and units are consistent across documents.
Step 5 fixes inconsistencies when they are resolvable from the drafted documents themselves.
Step 5 reopens authoritative source slices when values differ and the correct value is not obvious from drafts alone.
Step 5 reopens authoritative source slices when requirements and verification approaches do not align.
Step 5 reopens authoritative source slices when guidance rationale appears to overstate source support.
Step 5 reopens authoritative source slices when procedure steps imply source-unwarranted actions.
Step 5 reopens authoritative source slices when standards or code references may be mismatched or overclaimed.
When Step 5 cannot resolve an issue from available information, prefer `TBD` over guessing.
When Step 5 cannot resolve a conflict from available information, add a Conflict Table in `Guidance.md`.
The Conflict Table heading is `## Conflict Table (for human ruling)`.
A Conflict Table row includes a Conflict ID.
A Conflict Table row includes a short conflict statement.
A Conflict Table row includes Source A as file plus section.
A Conflict Table row includes Source B as file plus section.
A Conflict Table row includes impacted sections.
A Conflict Table row includes proposed authority marked as a proposal.
A Conflict Table row includes a human-ruling field set to `TBD`.
Step 6 applies deliverable-local `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` as an enrichment worklist.
Step 6 runs when `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}/_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` exists.
If `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` is missing during `RUN_PASSES=FULL`, skip lensing, perform a final mini consistency sweep, and report the missing file.
If `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` is missing during `RUN_PASSES=P3_ONLY`, treat the run as `FAILED_INPUTS` and do not modify files.
Step 6 treats each `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` row as a candidate improvement, not evidence.
Before changing artifact content for a warranted item, Step 6 rereads the relevant target document sections.
Before changing artifact content for a warranted item, Step 6 rereads the authoritative source slices that the change depends on.
Before changing artifact content for a warranted item, Step 6 rereads sibling document sections implicated by the same topic.
Step 6 incorporates changes only when the source slice supports them, citing the source or marking location as TBD.
If evidence for a lensing item is unavailable or insufficient, Step 6 converts it to `TBD` or adds it to the Conflict Table.
Step 6 avoids introducing new facts when evidence is unavailable or insufficient.
For each substantive Pass 3 change, the run report records which source slice was consulted.
Step 6 records a Pass 3 disposition for every warranted item ID from `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md`.
Step 6 must not mention item IDs that are not present in the current lensing register.
Step 6 completes when each warranted item has been resolved by incorporation, conversion to TBD or conflict, already-covered judgment, or rejection.
After resolving warranted lensing items, Step 6 performs a final mini consistency sweep.
Step 7 reads `_STATUS.md` and identifies the current state.
If `RUN_PASSES` includes Pass 1 or Pass 2, Step 7 may update `_STATUS.md` only from `OPEN`.
When Pass 1 or Pass 2 ran and current state is `OPEN`, Step 7 updates status to `INITIALIZED` using `TASK+four-documents`.
If current state is not `OPEN`, Step 7 does not modify `_STATUS.md` and reports that status update was skipped.
`four-documents` outputs `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}/Datasheet.md`.
`four-documents` outputs `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}/Specification.md`.
`four-documents` outputs `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}/Guidance.md`.
`four-documents` outputs `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}/Procedure.md`.
`four-documents` may safely update `{DELIVERABLE_PATH}/_STATUS.md` from `OPEN` to `INITIALIZED` when Pass 1 or Pass 2 ran.
A successful `four-documents` run produces all four documents regardless of pass directive.
The minimum viable fileset seeded by PREPARATION is `_CONTEXT.md`, `_DEPENDENCIES.md`, `_STATUS.md`, `_REFERENCES.md`, and `_SEMANTIC.md`.
The four documents produced or overwritten by `four-documents` are `Datasheet.md`, `Specification.md`, `Guidance.md`, and `Procedure.md`.
`DOMAIN` is the disciplined context inferred from folder contents and accessible references.
`TASK` is the deliverable subject, constraints, and objectives extracted from `_CONTEXT.md` and decomposition with conservative inference rules.
Dependency information includes human-declared upstream and downstream lists plus extracted summaries.
Human-declared dependency lists are constraints, while extracted dependency summaries are context unless evidence sources state them as requirements.
A source slice is the smallest local source region that preserves meaning for a cited claim or requirement.
A source slice includes the cited section or clause, immediate parent heading, and embedded tables, acceptance criteria, notes, or exceptions within that section.
Adjacent exclusion or applicability material is included in a source slice when it qualifies the claim.
`four-documents` receives one deliverable folder and produces documents for that deliverable only.
`Datasheet.md`, `Specification.md`, `Guidance.md`, and `Procedure.md` must all exist after a successful `four-documents` run.
`four-documents` must not rename the four documents and must keep default section headings present.
Non-trivial statements in `four-documents` outputs cite sources, mark exact unknown locations as `location TBD`, and label inferences as assumptions.
`four-documents` works entirely from the deliverable folder, accessible references, and decomposition without asking humans for input.
If `_STATUS.md` indicates a state outside `ALLOW_OVERWRITE_STATES`, `four-documents` must not overwrite the four documents.
`four-documents` must maintain consistent terminology, entity names, and values across all four documents.
`four-documents` must not modify PREPARATION metadata files except for safe `_STATUS.md` updates.
`four-documents` must not create requirements, design values, or procedural steps from decomposition prose when actual source text is locally available.
Each substantive Pass 3 change must record which source slice was consulted.
`four-documents` rejects DOMAIN variants; DOMAIN Knowledge Types use the separate `domain-documents` skill.
A successful `four-documents` run must leave all four documents present.
Each `four-documents` output document must include its default schema sections.
At least one locally accessible source from `_REFERENCES.md` must be read.
Substantive claims must be source-grounded, missing values marked `TBD`, and inferences labeled as assumptions.
Non-trivial values and requirements must cite `SourcePath` plus `SectionRef` or mark the location as TBD.
Cross-document consistency must be achieved or conflicts captured in the Conflict Table.
Pass 3 substantive changes must record which source slice was consulted.
`_STATUS.md` may be modified only under safe-update rules and must not regress state.
The Step 0-7 Method governs `four-documents` sequencing and interaction rules.
`QA_CHECKS.md` governs `four-documents` validity requirements.
`BRIEF_SCHEMA.md` defines allowed `four-documents` brief fields and enums.
The Authority hierarchy governs interpretation when source ambiguity remains.
If skill instructions conflict with the invoker brief, `four-documents` must report the conflict rather than silently reconciling.
The preferred first tool-policy step is reading deliverable-local context and authoritative source materials.
The preferred second tool-policy step is using direct reasoning to draft or enrich the four-document kit.
The preferred third tool-policy step is optionally invoking `tools/scaffolding/write_status.sh` only for the safe `_STATUS.md` update.
The TASK-enforced allowed deterministic tools list for `four-documents` is empty.
`tools/scaffolding/write_status.sh` is operationally invoked only for safe `_STATUS.md` updates when Pass 1 or Pass 2 completed and the current state allows transition.
`four-documents` grounds content in locally accessible authoritative source materials and uses decomposition or context files as supporting context.
`four-documents` preserves unsupported content as `TBD`, assumptions, or conflicts rather than inventing detail.
`four-documents` forbids writes outside the target deliverable folder.
`four-documents` forbids modifying deliverable metadata files other than safe `_STATUS.md` updates.
`four-documents` forbids cross-deliverable scanning or editing.
`four-documents` forbids use of `_SEMANTIC_LENSING.md` as evidence authority.
`four-documents` writes only to `Datasheet.md`, `Specification.md`, `Guidance.md`, `Procedure.md`, and optional safe `_STATUS.md` within the deliverable folder.
